subject: fix(xpu): preserve functional batch-invariant residual RMSNorm
requirement: The optional request-stable XPU residual RMSNorm helper returns two independent outputs, preserves its input tensors and weights, adds in FP32 before reducing and weighting, and uses the same row-local reduction order across batch sizes. The scoped AEON GemmaRMSNorm caller still calls the helper on the final fork tip. The RedHat DFlash2 production profile does not activate it.
upstream_coverage: At 62d4bc3, vllm/model_executor/determinism/batch_invariant.py:1106-1113 unconditionally passes a residual to ops.fused_add_rms_norm and returns the input tensors. Upstream commits 57371c4e28, ba2d99fd4a and 829902026f update other functions in this file; the old-to-new diff leaves the helper untouched.

vllm/model_executor/layers/layernorm.py:RMSNorm.forward_xpu uses the native IR implementation for its own batch-invariant residual path. vllm/ir/ops/layernorm.py:fused_add_rms_norm uses FP32 addition and PyTorch mean, then rounds to the weight dtype before multiplication. This covers some ownership/precision needs but supplies no fixed reduction tree and does not fix the separate helper called directly by the fork's GemmaRMSNorm.request_invariant_apply_once. Neither alternate implementation changed between 0.33 and 0.34.

At 6a1ec18, csrc/torch_bindings.cpp:34 registers the mutable fused_add_rms_norm XPU operation. csrc/layernorm.cpp:772 changes max block size at 256 tokens, adds in scalar_t in its scalar/vector variants and writes through both input pointers. layernorm.cpp has identical blob fd504487cfff6257859966e1a1084ad963f2a559 in old and new kernel releases.
minimum_residual: Replay the XPU-only fixed-tree Triton helper, residual dispatch and regression tests intact. Preserve upstream's non-XPU dispatch and the normal RMSNorm.forward_xpu IR path. No new operator or native schema is needed.
dependencies: Later vLLM fork commit 066206bafe adds the scoped request-stability caller. Subsequent fork commits do not change batch_invariant.py; no folds or paired kernel edits are needed for this fix.

observed: git apply --check of the assigned patch succeeded against the isolated unpatched v0.34.0 checkout. Compared exact old/new helper diffs, caller implementations and kernel blob IDs.
Historical evidence ../rebase-v033-20261108/gpu/gpu-rmsnorm.json records seven passing tests with the installed v0.33 package on the B70.
candidate_pending: Run test_non_xpu_residual_rms_norm_preserves_native_dispatch and the full parameter matrix of test_xpu_residual_rms_norm_is_functional_and_batch_invariant against the rebuilt v0.34 package, including noncontiguous operands, FP32/absent weights and the 255/256/257 row boundary.
Qualify optional request-stability mode independently before making model-level claims.
validation.limits: Source review only for v0.34. No GPU execution or throughput claim.
